explanation: Both speed up skin turnover. Together they often cause redness, peeling and a damaged barrier. Use them on different nights.
Salicylic acid plus a retinoid is a lot of exfoliation at once and can leave skin raw and dry. Alternate nights instead.
Benzoyl peroxide can break down some retinoids, and the pair is very drying. Use benzoyl peroxide in the morning and the retinoid at night.
Pure vitamin C works best at a low pH, while retinoids can make skin more reactive. Layering both often stings. Vitamin C in the morning, retinoid at night.
Two low-pH products layered together can sting and irritate. Space them out, for example vitamin C in the morning and acids at night.
Stacking acidic vitamin C with salicylic acid can be too much for many skin types. Use them at different times of day.
Benzoyl peroxide is an oxidiser and can make vitamin C less effective. Keep them at different times of day.
Some products combine these on purpose at low strengths. Using a separate strong AHA and BHA together can over-exfoliate, so watch for tightness and stinging.
Exfoliating acids plus benzoyl peroxide is very drying and can irritate. Use them on different days or different times.
Both are strong acne-fighters. Together they can over-dry and inflame skin. Pick one per routine.
Pure vitamin C and copper peptides can make each other less effective. Use them at different times of day.
Strong acids can destabilise copper peptides. Keep them in separate routines for best results.
Not harmful, but both can be demanding on sensitive skin. Many people alternate nights.
Using two retinoids at once mostly adds irritation without adding much benefit. Stick to one.
Drying alcohol plus exfoliating acids can leave skin feeling tight and irritated. Keep an eye out for flaking.
